name: live_age_on_nullable_operand_is_null
description: AGE over a nullable operand is observed NULL against a live engine, not merely asserted from the model -- the #163 gap: no live fixture exercised AGE at all, so a fix that only changed the analyzer's model of AGE(NOW(), NULL) could regress silently. AGE is PostgreSQL-only (no MySQL/MariaDB/SQLite/MSSQL/Oracle equivalent that this suite's single shared query_sql could target), so this fixture runs on postgresql alone.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE accounts (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ);
query_sql:
-- @name AgeLive
-- @returns :many
SELECT id, AGE(NOW(), deleted_at) AS elapsed FROM accounts ORDER BY id

columns.name: elapsed
columns.note: deleted_at is nullable, so AGE(NOW(), deleted_at) is nullable

default: INSERT INTO accounts (id, deleted_at) VALUES (1, now() - interval '1 day')
INSERT INTO accounts (id, deleted_at) VALUES (2, NULL)
